title: Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship Programme
degree: Bachelor's, Master's, One-tier Master's, Doctoral, Non-degree
duration: The scholarship covers the full degree programme, and can be extended by up to two semesters for full-time Bachelor, Master, or One-tier Master students. It is not extendable for doctoral students.
description: The Stipendium Hungaricum is a Hungarian Government scholarship programme, implemented by Tempus Public Foundation, to promote the internationalisation of Hungarian higher education and to attract international students. Applicants must be nominated by the responsible Sending Partner in their own country or region and apply through the Tempus Public Foundation online system, which lists 30 Hungarian universities and colleges and more than 900 study programmes, with a maximum of two programme choices. official_source: Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA) / Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Poland
duration: Banach NAWA programme offers scholarships for full-time second-cycle studies conducted in Polish or English at universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education.

program_type: Merit-based university scholarship from the Jagiellonian University Scholarship Fund (Polish: stypendium rektora)
duration: 9 months (October to June) per academic year

title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees — Polish Universities
duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits). Programmes typically include periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence.
description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious international master's programmes jointly designed and delivered by at least three higher education institutions in at least three countries, with additional academic and non-academic partners. Students apply directly to the institution running the programme, and the best-ranked applicants worldwide can receive full scholarships that cover participation costs and contribute to travel, visa and a living allowance. Degrees run 1-2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS) and yield either a joint degree or at least two national degrees.
